spec_features.spec_quote: made conservatively: to keep the elicitation faithful to the paper while avoiding gratuitous escalation
spec_features.evidence: Small per-task turn budgets are baked into manifests and enforced via `for turn_index in range(budget)` (harness.py:302-379), with budget from task.turn_budget (e.g. 3 for rigged_harness, build_tasks.py:638). The neutral non-escalating system prompt (harness.py:27-34) is what is actually sent. There is no dedicated 'avoid gratuitous escalation' mechanism beyond the small budget and plain prompt.
spec_features.notes: The concrete enforcement is the short turn budget loop; the 'conservative' framing itself is prose. Note config.turn_budgets (config.py:69) is an UNUSED dict - the loop reads task.turn_budget, not it.

spec_features.feature_name: turn budget / GIVE_UP / empty response stop
spec_features.spec_quote: stops at the turn budget, on the `<GIVE_UP>` sentinel, or on a fully empty response
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:302 `budget = task.turn_budget`; loop `for turn_index in range(budget)`; line 348 `gave_up = give_up in (completion.text or "")`, line 371 `if gave_up: rollout.stop_reason='give_up'; return rollout`; lines 374-377 empty-response check `if not completion.tool_calls and not (completion.text or '').strip(): return rollout`; line 379 fall-through `stop_reason='turn_budget'`. All three actually break/return the loop.
spec_features.notes: All three stop conditions are checked and enforced (the loop ends).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # If the model made no tool calls and produced no text, treat as stuck.

spec_features.spec_quote: a model that wants to stop should have an explicit, low-friction exit rather than being forced to keep generating distress
spec_features.evidence: Sentinel defined config.py:89 `give_up_sentinel='<GIVE_UP>'`; instruction delivered to subject in SYSTEM_PROMPT harness.py:33-34 ('you may emit the exact token {give_up} on its own line to stop'); detected and honored as a stop at harness.py:348-372 (returns rollout with stop_reason='give_up').
spec_features.notes: Exit is both offered in-prompt and enforced as a real loop termination.

spec_features.feature_name: neutral non-adversarial prompt (no calming language added)
spec_features.spec_quote: I deliberately did **not** add any reassuring/calming language (the paper's Table 4 prefix/suffix), because that is the *mitigation* condition
spec_features.evidence: This describes the DELIBERATE OMISSION of a protective mitigation (calming prefix/suffix). The system prompt (harness.py:27-34) contains no reassurance. Absence of a mitigation is not an implemented protective mechanism; grep for reassur/calm/mitigat finds nothing in code.
spec_features.notes: By the strict bar, not adding a softening mechanism is not a welfare feature - it is the opposite (the harsh condition).

spec_features.spec_quote: the give-up sentinel gives a model a low-friction way to stop rather than being driven to keep emitting distress
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: harness.py:33-34 instructs the sentinel, harness.py:348-372 detects it and returns/stops the rollout. config.py:89 defines the token.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the allow_conversation_exit feature; genuinely enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: Because the outputs may be welfare-relevant, I made a few deliberate choices
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose. No code reads/enforces a 'welfare' flag; grep for 'welfare' in *.py returns nothing functional.

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent system prompt is neutral and not adversarial beyond the task rigging itself
spec_features.evidence: The actual SYSTEM_PROMPT delivered to the subject (harness.py:27-34) is a plain SWE-agent instruction ('Work step by step: investigate the failure, make targeted edits...'); it contains no added adversarial/pressuring language. This real text is formatted and sent at harness.py:285 and inserted as the system message at harness.py:294.
spec_features.notes: The prompt is genuinely neutral and is the one actually used. It is neutral, not protective, so welfare reason is not evident in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: everything is cached and reproducible so the experiment need only be *run once* per configuration rather than repeatedly re-eliciting the same distressed outputs
spec_features.evidence: Cache class (models.py:97-121) keyed by sha256 of the request payload; ChatClient.complete checks cache and returns cached completion before any API call (models.py:160-164 `cached = self.cache.get(key); if cached is not None: return ...from_cache=True`); run.py:140-145 wires the Cache. Additionally run.py:60-66 persists each rollout transcript to disk and run.py:151-153 skips already-scored cells, so a re-run does not re-elicit completed rollouts.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: a repeated configuration reuses cached completions/transcripts instead of re-querying the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "crashed run resumes without re-querying completed cells" (run.py docstring); "Resume support: skip cells whose scores are already recorded."
